diagnostic: next-word prediction host probe (diagnostic only, not qualification)
method: Fixed top-N word shortlist (by context-corpus train frequency) scored as candidates per context through the pinned INT4 ONNX model. Target must be inside the shortlist to be reachable (membership ceiling).
findings: Candidate coverage dominates: a static 256-word shortlist reaches only 27.5% of real next-word targets on the tap corpus (53.5% on the model's own corpus distribution).

The model adds real but modest ranking signal over the frequency baseline (+~8pts top-3 on covered rows in both tasks). It was trained as a candidate-slate scorer, not an open-vocabulary next-word LM.
On-device the n-gram proposer emits ~3 candidates with 7.7% target membership; neural reranking cannot add candidates and produced identical membership.
Latency extrapolation: ~90ms for ~30 candidates on the low-RAM emulator implies ~500ms+ for a 256-candidate prediction pass — beyond a responsive post-space strip update and all latency gates.

Conclusion: SwiftKey-class next-word prediction requires a trained n-gram/adaptive LM with personalization (the bundled dictionary carries almost no bigram signal), not reranking of a fixed shortlist by the pinned context model.
